- [Cloudflare 让 1.1.1.1 免于罚款：赢在程序，而 Quad9 可能因为同一个理由退出法国](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-09_cloudflare-1111-france-piracy-blocking/): Translation+analysis of TorrentFreak's report on the Paris Judicial Court's 17 September 2026 decision rejecting Canal+ requests for daily penalties against Cloudflare. Covers the April 2026 orders requiring Cloudflare to block 21 Formula 1 and 16 MotoGP domains, which covered both the DNS resolver and the CDN but prescribed no method, requiring only that access from France be prevented by any effective means; Canal+'s May request for 50,000 EUR per day per site still accessible plus the same for each new site Arcom reports; and Canal+'s claim that Cloudflare circumvented the measures by implementing only through its CDN, leaving just three of 21 domains blocked (three of 16 in the MotoGP case) with two of those three returning a week later via a different CDN or a mirror. Sets out the court's reasoning: the fact that Cloudflare blocks only through the CDN when the site uses that service is undisputed; Cloudflare argued CDN blocking is incomparably more effective and that its public resolver's architecture does not permit blocking, making such measures unreasonable; and the three-judge panel treated Canal+'s own 72.6 percent blocking figure as evidence of genuine willingness to help, though the ruling never explains how that percentage relates to the three-out-of-21 figure - the piece flags this unexplained inconsistency as an appealable weak point since the court's conclusion rests on statistics provided by the party seeking penalties. Also covers the responsibility boundary the court drew (Cloudflare cannot be held responsible when site owners switch CDNs or redirect to mirrors, and it is up to Canal+ to pursue the new intermediary and report mirrors to Arcom) and the rejection of Canal+'s UPC Telekabel Wien argument, with the Paris court reading that ruling as requiring only reasonable measures rather than effective blocking. Notes that 1.1.1.1 remains untouched and that Cloudflare's transparency reports repeatedly state it has never blocked content through its public DNS resolver despite French and Italian orders, while geoblocking through the CDN reached 662 domains under seven orders in the first half of 2025 and 1,238 domains under a single order in the second half. Explains the asymmetry that gives the ruling its narrow scope: Quad9 faces a comparable and potentially bankrupting penalty request from beIN Sports for refusing to block on its resolver, with a figure up to 580,000 EUR per day, but unlike Cloudflare it has no CDN through which to demonstrate alternative compliance, so the precedent offers it no protection. Adds supplementary context on the escalating French framework with sources: ISP orders from 2022, alternative DNS resolvers in 2024, 203 domains blocked by five VPNs in May 2025, the Paris Court of Appeal's 27 March 2026 rejection of five appeals covering Google Public DNS, Cloudflare and Cisco OpenDNS under Article L.333-10 of the Sports Code (where the court held that a service's neutral and passive character is beside the point, that the existence of VPN workarounds does not make filtering useless, and that Cisco's 64 person-weeks of implementation cost did not persuade), and the Conseil d'Etat's 15 July 2026 decision (no. 509579) compelling Cloudflare to enforce Arcom's blocking of EU-sanctioned Russian media addresses while declining to refer the DSA Article 9 question to the CJEU - a reminder that the administrative and judicial tracks produce opposite outcomes for the same company. Covers Cloudflare's alternative proposal to the European Commission's Counterfeit and Piracy Watch List consultation (global public DNS resolvers should not be used to block access, and its real-time stream mitigation lets vetted rightsholders flag infringing streams disrupted within seconds without DNS or IP blocking), comparing domain-level blocking with real-time stream disruption, and noting an EU-commissioned study's conclusion that the goal should be real-time blocking within 30 minutes. Closes with the judgement that Cloudflare won on the wording of a method-agnostic order rather than on any principle protecting DNS resolvers, that deciding a compliance obligation based on whether the defendant happens to operate a second business is a questionable design, and that DNS-level blocking is being eroded by both its limited effectiveness and the spread of encrypted DNS.

- [Quick Share 什么都好，除了它没有 Linux 客户端：手机与 PC 互传的四种走法](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-09_quickshare-linux-android-file-transfer/): Research+analysis answering whether an Android phone and a Linux PC can transfer files via Google's Quick Share. Covers what Quick Share is (the 2024-era merger of Google's Nearby Share with Samsung's Quick Share, built into Play Services on Android 6+, with Samsung devices using their own settings surface): Bluetooth/BLE for discovery and authentication, then a direct Wi-Fi link (Wi-Fi Direct or Wi-Fi Aware / NAN) for the actual transfer, which is why multi-gigabyte files move quickly without cloud upload. Notes that Android has shipped platform Wi-Fi Aware support since 8.0 and that Android 17 moves Wi-Fi Aware control logic out of firmware into wpa_supplicant and the framework. Documents the official platform coverage: Android, Chromebook and Windows (Quick Share for Windows requires 64-bit Windows 10+; ARM-based devices need Windows 11+; Samsung PCs must use Samsung's build since Google's no longer supports them), and the central finding that there is no official Linux desktop client - ChromeOS is the only place Quick Share ships in a Linux-based form, while general Linux distributions are served only by third-party reverse-engineered clients. Details those clients: Packet (GTK4 + Rust, available on Flathub, AUR and nixpkgs, send and receive, Nautilus context menu, autostart, tray icon, D-Bus API) and rquickshare (Rust, .deb/.rpm/AppImage/Nix/AUR, also macOS), plus the limits both share because only the Wi-Fi LAN medium is implemented: Bluetooth must be enabled, devices must sit on a Wi-Fi network with mDNS, Android's mDNS service is advertised only intermittently (rquickshare broadcasts a Bluetooth advertisement to prompt it, which requires Bluetooth on the PC), firewalls can block the port unless a static port is enabled, and pinning down a receive entry point on Android may require an activity shortcut to com.google.android.gms.nearby.sharing.ReceiveSurfaceActivity - with a note that Samsung modified Quick Share and the workaround may not hold. Covers the AirDrop interoperability accurately: it needs the Quick Share Extension and applies to Pixel 8a, Pixel 9 and Pixel 10 families plus selected Samsung, Xiaomi, OPPO, vivo, OnePlus, HONOR, Transsion and Motorola models (Pixel 8 and 8 Pro long excluded, with staged rollout from late 2026), requires the receiving Apple device to set AirDrop to Everyone for 10 minutes, and for unsupported devices the QR-code path uploads end-to-end encrypted files to Google servers for 24 hours with caps of 1,000 files, 10 GB per file and 10 GB per day. Compares the alternatives for the Linux side: LocalSend (own LAN protocol, app on both ends, widest cross-platform coverage including iOS, no Google services dependency), KDE Connect (notification and clipboard integration rather than a pure file mover), and USB/adb for bulk transfers. Closes with the China-specific reality that domestic Android devices generally route near-field sharing through the Mutual Transmission Alliance (founded August 2019 by Xiaomi, OPPO and vivo, joined by HONOR in February 2025, BLE discovery plus Wi-Fi P2P, up to about 20 MB/s), which has no PC client and does not open its protocol, so phone-to-Linux-PC transfers are best served by LocalSend or a cable.
  - Key topics: Quick Share, Nearby Share, Samsung Quick Share, Android file transfer, Linux desktop, Packet, nozwock, rquickshare, Flathub, Flatpak, LocalSend, KDE Connect, Bluetooth LE discovery, Wi-Fi Direct, Wi-Fi Aware, NAN, mDNS, AirDrop interoperability, Quick Share Extension, Pixel 8a, QR code cloud transfer, Mutual Transmission Alliance, 互传联盟, adb, MTP, 原创

- [zram 重构读写流：内存省下「几十到几百 KB」，但真正的看点是消除优先级反转](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-06_zram-streams-rework/): Translation+analysis of Sergey Senozhatsky's (Google Chrome/Chromium team) zram rework patch series on LKML. The zcomp redesign splits the compression stream into per-CPU read streams and per-CPU write streams, eliminating a priority inversion under preemptible zram where a higher-priority Reader preempts a Writer holding the stream lock and then blocks on that same lock — safe to split because the read (decompress) and write (compress) paths never touch each other's buffers (idea credited to Barry Song). The final patch then makes recompression use a singleton compression context while keeping per-CPU decompression contexts, since secondary streams are only used by recompression which is serialized by the device lock (single-threaded) yet was still allocated per-CPU — saving notable memory with zstd, deflate and lz4hc. Savings are stated as 'double digits KB to triple digits KB' per-context/per-CPU and compound across cores and contexts. Includes the author's original quoting, the distinction between 'noticeable improvements on synthetic tests' and the more bullish media framing, kernel-doc context on CONFIG_ZRAM_MULTI_COMP recompression (up to 4 algorithms, /sys/block/zramX/recompress with type=idle|huge|huge_idle, threshold, priority), and a real-machine audit (zstd selected, 2.4G used of 7.7G) with mm_stat-ratio self-check guidance.
  - Key topics: zram, zcomp, per-CPU streams, read/write stream decoupling, priority inversion, preemptible zram, secondary compression streams, recompression, singleton context, zstd, deflate, lz4hc, lzo-rle, CONFIG_ZRAM_MULTI_COMP, recomp_algorithm, memory prices, memory savings, LKML patch review, mm_stat compression ratio, swap on zram

- [一个布尔值把内网服务变成了公网服务：把通配监听收回内网（socat 桥模式）](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-06_wildcard-listen-to-lan-only/): 原创实操复盘（非译文）。核心问题：很多服务只提供两个监听选项——只听 `127.0.0.1`，或听所有网卡（`0.0.0.0` / `*`）；**没有「只听内网」这一档**。本文给出通用解法：让服务退回只听回环，再用 `socat` 在指定内网地址上补一个口。触发场景：代理客户端的 `httpProxyListenLAN: true` 让它绑定 `*:8888`，而 `*` 在 Linux 上**同时含 IPv4 `0.0.0.0` 与 IPv6 `[::]`** —— 在有公网 IPv6 的机器上等于把内网服务直接暴露给整个互联网（实测从外部 `curl --socks5-hostname [<pub-v6>]:1080 https://example.com` 返回 **200**）。根因（从二进制提取 JSON tag 证实）：该服务只有布尔开关 `httpProxyListenLAN`（无「绑定指定地址」选项），日志字符串也只有两个硬编码地址 `listening to socks5://0.0.0.0:%d` 与 `listening to socks5://127.0.0.1:%d`。解法三步：① 服务配置改回 `...ListenLAN: false` 只听 `127.0.0.1`；② 新建 systemd 单元 `ExecStart=/usr/bin/socat TCP4-LISTEN:8888,bind=<LAN_IP>,fork,reuseaddr TCP4:127.0.0.1:8888`，用 `After=`/`Requires=` 关联原服务；③ `systemctl daemon-reload && restart && enable --now`，然后 `ss -tlnH | grep 8888` 验证。三个实测要点：**① `bind=<具体内网 IP>` 不会产生任何 `[::]` 监听**（对照实验 IPv6 监听数 = 0），而写成 `bind=0.0.0.0` 就会重新暴露、前功尽弃；**② 同一端口可在 `127.0.0.1` 与内网 IP 上共存**（内核按「地址+端口」组合绑定套接字，这是方案可行性的前提）；**③ 转发链全程在回环内**（`socat` 的后端是 `127.0.0.1`，不出机器、不经网络接口）。改造效果：本机可用 + 内网可用 + **公网 IPv6 不可达**。适用泛化：任何只有「全网/本机」二选一的服务（某些数据库的 `bind-address` 不生效、开发服务器 `--host 0.0.0.0` 等）。附通配监听审计命令 `ss -tlnH | awk '{print $4}' | grep -E '^\*:|^\[::\]:|^0\.0\.0\.0:'`。核心教训：**`0.0.0.0` 和 `*` 不是「内网」而是「所有接口」**，在有公网 IPv6 的机器上等价于公网开放；改完必须用 `grep -c '\[::\]:'` 验证，直觉不可靠。
  - Key topics: 暴露面收敛, attack surface reduction, 通配监听, wildcard listen, 0.0.0.0, [::], IPv6 exposure, socat, TCP4-LISTEN, bind, fork, reuseaddr, systemd unit, After/Requires, 127.0.0.1, loopback-only, LAN-only binding, 端口共存, 地址+端口组合, mieru, httpProxyListenLAN, JSON tag 提取, strings 二进制分析, 公网 IPv6, 代理暴露, curl --socks5-hostname, ss -tlnH 审计, 安全加固

- [万物皆隧道（续）：给香橙派接上 Cloudflare 零信任 SSH，每个访问端一张 3 分钟证书](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-06_orange-pi-cloudflare-zero-trust-ssh/): 原创架构复盘（非译文），《万物皆隧道》续集。上一篇假设有公网可达入口（IPv6），这篇解决更硬的约束：**公网 IPv4 根本不归你**——登进光猫发现 WAN = `100.64.12.34`（落在 `100.64.0.0/10`，RFC 6598 CGNAT），而实际出口是另一个地址，证明上游还有运营商 NAT，**是三重 NAT**。因此 IPv4 端口映射物理不可能、DDNS 更新 A 记录毫无意义。方案对比：**mTLS 三处不可行**（① 官方文档：Access mTLS 仅 Enterprise/pay-as-you-go，不含 Free，用户账号是 `teams_free`；② `cloudflared access ssh` 无任何客户端证书参数，只有 header/service-token-id/service-token-secret；③ mTLS 语义是 HTTP(S) 握手，而 SSH 隧道走 WebSocket 升级）；**Service Token** 虽 Free 可用但默认 `8760h`（一年）长期凭据，泄露即长期可用；最终选 **Cloudflare Access 短时 SSH 证书**。搭建要点：① **用 `cloudflared tunnel login` 的浏览器授权建隧道**，绕开 API token 缺 `Cloudflare Tunnel: Edit` 的问题（POST cfd_tunnel 报 `10000 Authentication error`），全程在服务器上完成，不依赖 API token、也不用本机做代理；② **ingress 两个必须项**——service 必须是 `ssh://localhost:22` 而非 `tcp://`，且必须写 `originRequest.access.audTag`（含 Access app 的 aud）+ `teamName` + `required: true`，否则 Access 保护的非 HTTP 路由会卡在 `Connection timed out during banner exchange`（症状极具误导性，看着像网络问题实为鉴权未配完）；③ **SSH CA 端点是 per-application**（`POST /accounts/{id}/access/apps/{app_id}/ca`，账号级 `access/gateway_ca` 报 Authentication error）；④ dashboard API **GET 可用但 POST 常返 403 text/html**，实战用 dashboard UI 的「Generate certificate」按钮成功生成 CA；⑤ **短时证书的 principal 是邮箱本地部分**（`me@example.net` → `me`），与服务器登录用户（`myuser`）不匹配时 sshd 会拒绝，需配 `AuthorizedPrincipalsFile`（`/etc/ssh/authorized_principals/%u` 内容写 `me`）做映射，**无需新建用户**；同时 `TrustedUserCAKeys` 指向 CA 公钥。短时证书实测数据：`Valid: from 2026-10-06T00:11:51 to 00:15:51` = **4 分钟**（含时钟余量）；官方博客原话 **3 分钟**，并明确「3 分钟窗口**只约束认证阶段**，SSH 会话本身可以任意长（arbitrarily longer than 3 minutes）」。证书还带 `permit-port-forwarding`/`permit-pty` 扩展。安全收益：无长期密钥需生成/分发/备份/轮换/吊销，证书 3 分钟后自动失效，且走**出口-only 隧道**服务器零入站端口。非技术坑（最有价值的一条）：**本机设备级出网过滤器专拦 Go 编译的二进制**，`cloudflared`（Go）的 WebSocket 因此静默卡死，而同环境 `python`/`curl` 完全正常——一开始被误判成 DNS 超时；放行/关闭 OpenSnitch 后立刻 `HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols`。教训：排查「某程序连不上网」先做对照实验——**换一个非同类实现试同一目标**，若 python 通而 Go 不通，问题就不在网络层而在该程序被区别对待。最终形态为三条路径并存：`pi-ssh.example.net`（CF 隧道+短时证书，IPv4/IPv6 通用）、`pi6.example.net`（IPv6 直通，最快）、`pi.lan`（LAN 直连）。
  - Key topics: 零信任, Zero Trust, Cloudflare Tunnel, cloudflared, Cloudflare Access, SSH, 短时证书, short-lived certificate, SSH CA, TrustedUserCAKeys, AuthorizedPrincipalsFile, principal 映射, mTLS 不可行, Service Token, teams_free, CGNAT, RFC 6598, 100.64.0.0/10, 三重 NAT, 光猫 WAN, DDNS 无意义, 端口映射不可能, tunnel login, cert.pem, tunnel create, tunnel route dns, ingress, ssh://, originRequest, audTag, teamName, banner exchange 超时, per-application CA, gateway_ca, dashboard API 403, cloudflared access ssh-gen, ssh-config --short-lived-cert, ProxyCommand, Match exec, Go 二进制出网被拦, OpenSnitch, 101 Switching Protocols, 对照实验

- [国庆回老家，万物皆隧道：把家里所有服务收敛到只剩一个 SSH 端口](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-05_all-services-over-one-ssh-tunnel/): 原创架构复盘（非译文）。一次假期前的网络改造：把本地 DNS/代理/远程桌面/RustDesk/模型网关全部收敛到 `127.0.0.1`，由一条 SSH 隧道按需拉取；跳板机（香橙派，aarch64）对公网**只留 22 端口**，其余服务一律只听回环。文中域名与 IP 均已脱敏。八组关键设计：(1) **服务只听 127.0.0.1，隧道来拉**——实测 loopback-only 服务可被 `ssh -L` 转发（`-L` 的「远端」是从跳板机视角解析的），因此不再需要 VLAN/内网 ACL/VPN；(2) **OpenSSH 10.3 (Debian 13) 拒绝绑定 IPv4 字面量**——`-L 127.0.0.1:...` 报 `getaddrinfo: Address family for hostname not supported`，须用 `-L [::1]:...`，再补 `socat TCP4-LISTEN:...,bind=127.0.0.1 ... TCP6:[::1]:...` 桥（这就是 RDP/RustDesk 要拆成两个 systemd 单元的原因）；(3) **统一可达性门禁 `tunnel-precheck`**——`ExecStartPre` 先探 22，别让 ssh 自己超时后靠 RestartSec 反复重试；必须探 **22 而非目标端口**，因为跳板机 unbound 绑 `0.0.0.0:53`（IPv4-only）而公网名是 AAAA-only，用 IPv6 探 :53 会 `connection refused` 误判服务已死；(4) **门禁解析必须跳过回环 nameserver**——本地 `resolv.conf` 首选 `127.0.0.1` 时，「启动隧道需解析跳板机、解析跳板机需隧道」形成自举死锁，解析顺序须为 `/etc/hosts` → 非回环 DNS → 系统解析器；(5) **`MODE=auto` 自动切换 LAN/WAN**——在家用 `socat` 直连不走 SSH，在外走公网 IPv6，网络变化时主动退出让 systemd 重启重新探测，客户端全程只认 `127.0.0.1`；(6) **端口归属要划清**——53 必须系统级单元（`man 5 resolv.conf` 的 `nameserver` 只接受纯 IP、无端口语法 + `ip_unprivileged_port_start=1024` 使绑 53 需特权，且 `systemctl --user` 加 `AmbientCapabilities` 报 `status=218/CAPABILITIES`），8888/8053 用户级即可，否则两个单元互抢监听端口；(7) **改 DNS 的三层保护**——只在隧道真正监听后写入（`wait-up` 轮询）、`127.0.0.1` 置顶但保留 DHCP DNS 兜底（glibc 按序回退）、`ExecStopPost` 摘除；(8) **UDP 不能直接走 `ssh -L`**——字节流会丢报文边界，需两端 `socat` 做流/报文转换，远端 socat 由 SSH 会话拉起随其退出，硬杀会留孤儿故需锚定 `pgrep` 预清理。安全实践：只留一个入口把攻击面从 N 个应用收敛到一个 OpenSSH；`BatchMode=yes` 纯公钥认证；**`HostKeyAlias` 让「pin 解析出的 IP」不削弱主机密钥校验**——本项目真实遭遇过 DNS 污染把跳板机域名解析到陌生境外地址，严格校验当场拒绝连接，挡下了向那台服务器发送 API key。
  - Key topics: SSH tunnel, ssh -L, port forwarding, 内网收敛, loopback-only, 127.0.0.1, socat, IPv4-IPv6 bridge, OpenSSH 10.3, getaddrinfo Address family not supported, systemd ExecStartPre, reachability precheck, DNS bootstrap deadlock, resolv.conf no port syntax, ip_unprivileged_port_start, AmbientCapabilities CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE, status=218, UDP over SSH, DNS over tunnel, unbound, MODE=auto, LAN/WAN auto-switch, location-dependent DNS, /etc/hosts nsswitch files dns, HostKeyAlias, DNS poisoning, attacks surface reduction, VLAN/ACL/VPN替代, RustDesk, RDP, remote desktop tunneling, model gateway tunnel, aarch64, Orange Pi

- [从 PSK 提取到私有引擎逆向：一次 Goodix 27c6:501d 指纹 Linux 适配的完整失败复盘](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-01_goodix-501d-linux-fingerprint-postmortem/): 原创复盘（非译文）。一台 H3C H3CBook Ultra 14T 在 Debian 13 / niri 下三天适配 Goodix `27c6:501d` 的完整记录，结论是**明确放弃**。技术全链：(1) **驱动家族误判**——先用 `djnz00/libfprint` 的 `goodixtls52xd`（52xd/G4 家族，PSK 是硬编码白盒常量），加 PID 后设备被认出但 TLS 握手被拒；从 libfprint 调试日志抠出设备真实 PSK 哈希填进 `goodix_52xd_pmk_hash_10034` 让 `memcmp` 通过，仍过不了握手——**哈希可比对 ≠ 能握手**。(2) **正确家族** = GM168SEC（固件 `GFUSB_GM168SEC_APP_10034`），用 `mrcook1e-ai/goodix-gm168` / `ejsergeev/libfprint-goodix-gm168sec` 集成树（patch 0001 capture + 0002 sigfm + 0003~0008 修复，需给两个驱动的 `id_table` 都加 `0x501d`）。(3) **PSK 提取**：GM168SEC 的 PSK 是 per-device、由 Windows 驱动首次联机时随机生成并用 DPAPI 密封写入 MCU NVRAM（`cmd 0xE4 / tag 0xbb010002` 读 324B sealed blob，前 20B 是 DPAPI 魔数 `01000000 d08c9ddf 0115d111 8c7a00c0 4fc297eb`；`tag 0xbb020001` 读 SHA-256(psk) 完整性哈希）。原 Win11 已重装、C 盘格式化、DPAPI 主密钥永久丢失，WINRE 恢复分区 `nvme0n1p4` 内的 `Winre.wim` 经 7z 核实**无 `Microsoft/Protect`**。解法 = **Win11 虚机 SPICE usbredir 直通重新 provision**：直通设备 → 装 H3C 官方驱动（`WbdiUsb.inf` 含 `USB\Vid_27C6&Pid_501D`；PSK 在驱动联机即生成，不需真划手指）→ 取消重定向回宿主 → root 跑 `img-capture` 读新 324B blob（sha256 变化证实覆盖）→ 虚机里 `gm168_unseal.ps1`（SYSTEM 账户 DPAPI）解出 **32 字节明文 PSK**。验证日志：`pre-shared key loaded` → `TLS handshake complete, cipher PSK-AES128-CBC-SHA256` → `INIT_NUM_STATES completed successfully` → `AWAIT_FINGER_ON`。(4) **FDT 阈值修正（卡三周的常量）**：驱动里的 finger-detection 阈值来自 589a（固件 10008）与 501d 不符——589a `1c 01 a4 00 a6 00 a4 00 a5 00`(35B, 164/166/164/165) vs 501d `9c 01 25 01 1f 01 27 01 21 01`(40B, 293/287/295/289)；Windows 还多发 `0x36`/`0x80` 两条 Linux 完全没有的命令。抓真值靠宿主 `usbmon`（`tcpdump -i usbmon3`，linktype 220）抓 Windows 经 SPICE 的明文流量，替换后**触摸立即被检测**（`finger_detected=1`）。注意 `0x32/0x34` 帧只有前 10 字节是固定阈值、其余是自适应增益，而 `set_param(0x90)` 反而该用原 589a 值。(5) **录入成功**：`enrollment validated: 14 presses, cluster 13, LOO pass 11`。(6) **匹配失败（真正卡点）**：SIGFM 在工作点 `TVERIFY=1000` 下，真手指分数 [554, 1845] 与陌生手指 [1067, 1091] **分布重叠**（真手指 #1 = 554 被拒、陌生手指 #1 = 1091 通过）；libfprint 默认 NBIS/Bozorth3 实测 `mindtct` 仅 **0.38 细节点/帧**（Bozorth3 至少要 2 个配对）→ 结构性不可用。根因是面积：80×64 @ 500dpi ≈ 13 mm²。(7) **Wine 方案（逆向私有引擎）**：从 H3C 驱动包提取 `GoodixEngineAdapter.dll`（1,176,792 B，PE32+ x64，29 个未混淆导出，**不导入 SGX**，依赖仅 KERNEL32/ADVAPI32/OLE32/OLEAUT32/WINMM/WS2_32/dbghelp/UCRT）。Wine 10.0 下 `LoadLibraryA` 成功、29 导出全解析、`WbioQueryEngineInterface` 返回 S_OK、vtable 是标准 WBDI `WINBIO_ENGINE_INTERFACE`（23 项，从结构体 +0x20 开始，magic `0x0000000200000003`、size `0x168`）。`EngineAdapterAttach` 入口能过（要求 `EngineParam+0x08` 为 **64 位** -1、`+0x38` 为 NULL），但 `_LogicAlgCreateContext(p, 1)` 的 memcpy size **硬编码为 1 字节**，且完整初始化需要 **7 个设备接口虚函数回调**（idx 11/12/15/16/17/19/20，其中 `_GetSensorAttribute` 会向 MCU 发 `cmd 0x442004`）——这层由 Windows WBDI 框架注入，Wine 无 WDF/WBDI 宿主，引擎日志报 `[engineadapter.cpp][EngineAdapterAttach :0552] invalid device state`。代价量化：mingw 编 x64 PE 仅 0.7s，但 **Wine 每次启动约 7.4s**（prefix 773MB），只能做成常驻 helper。(8) **虚机方案（WinBio API）**：Windows Hello 在 `win11-ltsc` 内**完美工作**（录入/识别/拒绝陌生手指），`WbioSrvc` 启动后 `WinBioEnumBiometricUnits` 用 **Factor=8**（`WINBIO_TYPE_FINGERPRINT`）返回 `hr=0, count=1`、`WinBioOpenSession` 返回 `handle=1`；引擎位于 `C:\Windows\System32\WinBioPlugIns\GoodixEngineAdapter.dll`（WBF 主动加载、拿得到完整 WBDI 环境）。但 `WinBioIdentify`/`WinBioCaptureSample` 返回 **`ACCESS_DENIED`**——Win11 安全策略只允许锁屏/登录流程触发采集，第三方进程无资格。宿主→虚机通道受限：无 qemu-ga 时 ping/445/5985/5986/22 全不通，仅 RDP 3389，需在 libvirt XML 补 `org.qemu.guest_agent.0` channel 后用 `virsh qemu-agent-command` 跑 PowerShell（`-ExecutionPolicy Bypass`）。结论：**协议层全通，算法层不可用**；三条绕过匹配的路（SIGFM 自研 / Wine 跑引擎 / 虚机 WinBio）分别死于分数重叠、缺 WBDI 宿主、安全策略拒绝。资产留档：libfprint 集成树 patch 链、`win-protocol/{GOLD.md,REFERENCE.md}` 501d 金标准协议、`RUNBOOK-planC.md`、`FINAL-TECHNICAL-REVIEW.md`（309 行）。可复用坑：`fprintd.service` 的 `ProtectSystem=strict`+`ProtectHome=true`（库须为 `/usr/lib` 实体文件、PSK bootstrap 不能走 fprintd）、Debian trixie udev 改名（`udev`→`libudev` 且无 `udevdir`）、`apt-mark hold` 锁死替换。
  - Key topics: Goodix, 27c6:501d, GM168SEC, GFUSB_GM168SEC_APP_10034, libfprint, fprintd, PAM, pam_fprintd, TLS-PSK, PSK, PMK hash, DPAPI, sealed blob, cmd 0xE4, tag 0xbb010002, tag 0xbb020001, WinRE/Winre.wim, SPICE usbredir, Win11 虚机, qemu-ga, usbmon, FDT 阈值, 589a vs 501d, SIGFM, NBIS/Bozorth3, minutiae, mindtct, GoodixEngineAdapter.dll, WBDI, WINBIO_ENGINE_INTERFACE, EngineAdapterAttach, EngineParam, _GetSensorAttribute, cmd 0x442004, Wine, UMDF, WinBio API, WinBioEnumBiometricUnits, WinBioOpenSession, ACCESS_DENIED, 逆向工程, 驱动适配, Debian trixie, niri, Wayland

- [Google 确认 ChromeOS 2034 年退场：10 年支持承诺照旧，但较新 Chromebook 可迁移到 Googlebook OS](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-29_chromeos-phase-out-2034-googlebook/): Translation+analysis of Ars Technica (2026-09-28) + 9to5Google (2026-09-28) + Google's official support page for Chrome Enterprise/Education. Google has now put ChromeOS's end date in writing: **ChromeOS devices will receive regular updates and security patches "through mid-2034"**, and **"many of our newest Chromebook devices will be eligible to transition over to Googlebook OS"** (specifically "newer commercial Chromebook models"); migration paths and device eligibility "soon." The 10-year support commitment is unchanged in wording but **redefined in substance**: for qualifying devices purchased today whose 10-year lifecycle **extends beyond 2034**, Google commits to supporting the **transition to Googlebook OS**, with many devices offering **direct migration paths** — i.e. 10 years is served by ChromeOS + Googlebook OS in relay, not by ChromeOS alone. Management experience for Googlebooks starts rolling out **H2 2027** (not available now). Google also says it remains "committed" to web developers despite more Android apps on Googlebooks. **Googlebook OS** is the **Android-based desktop OS** (codename **Aluminum OS**, successor to Chromebook); Wikipedia/PCWorld call it "basically Android for laptops" while Google avoids the word "Android." Hardware: 16GB RAM baseline, aluminum/magnesium, Snapdragon X Elite or Intel Core Ultra 3 (MediaTek Dimensity CX C10 Max supports the platform but unused at launch); **$899+** (up to $1,299); first models from Acer/Asus/Dell/HP/Lenovo; **launches 2026-10-04** (US), 10-05 in CA/UK/IE/FR/DE/AU; includes 12 months Google AI Pro + Gemini; **10-year software support** like Chromebooks. Timeline: 2026-05-12 announced (with Android 17) → 2026-09-21 preorders → 2026-10-04 launch → H2 2027 management rollout → **mid-2034 ChromeOS support ends**. The 2034 date previously appeared in **antitrust court testimony (Feb 2026)**: Google's lawyers said Aluminum won't be compatible with all existing Chromebook hardware, so ChromeOS must be maintained at least through 2033 to honor the 10-year commitment, with "timeline to phase out ChromeOS is 2034." Key takeaways: controlled sunset (not a brick), the 10-year promise quietly redefined, Googlebook is Android-for-laptops with Google avoiding the word, enterprises should wait for H2-2027 management + eligibility lists, and ChromeOS's exit means Google's laptop OS shifts from a (closed) Linux userland to an Android userland.
  - Key topics: ChromeOS, ChromeOS phase-out, mid-2034, Googlebook, Googlebook OS, Aluminum OS, Chromebook, Android-based desktop OS, Chrome Enterprise, Chrome Education, 10-year support, migration paths, court testimony, Snapdragon X Elite, Intel Core Ultra 3, Gemini
- [Chrome 都两周一个大版本了，信创浏览器还停在 120：内核版本碎片化才是信创的真难题](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-29_xinchuang-browser-kernel-lag/): Original industry analysis (Chinese Xinchuang / domestic-OS space). Frames the problem against **Chrome's cadence** — per Chromium's official release_cycle.md and Chrome for Developers blog, Chrome stable went 6 weeks → 4 weeks (M96, Sep 2021) → **2 weeks starting Chrome 153 (2026-09-08)**; Chrome 154 followed 2026-09-22; each 3-week-stabilized milestone still ships every 2 weeks via **overlapping pipelines**, plus **weekly security refreshes**. Community Chromium baseline is now **140–152** (Ungoogled-Chromium latest **152.0.7977.82**, 2026-09-04). Meanwhile Xinchuang browsers lag and **fragment**: deepin (UOS community) bundled browser stuck at **93** (2021), **统信 UOS 浏览器 at 108** (official, 2024-08), **360 信创版 at Chromium 120** (360 forum, 2025-09) while 360's Windows build already hit **140** — i.e. **1–3 years behind plus intra-ecosystem version fragmentation**. Root cause is structural, not laziness: (1) **certification/freeze** — an approved OS+browser+business-app+CA+国密 combo needs full re-validation on any kernel bump, and a 2-week kernel cadence outpaces cert cycles; (2) **国密 (SM2/3/4) + UKey + private CA** are deeply customized into the browser and must be re-ported each bump; (3) business systems coded to old kernel behavior (gov OA, e-seals, stream/office plugins) risk breaking on new kernels; (4) net result: stuck with **old-kernel security debt + new-web-feature incompatibility** simultaneously. Proposed pragmatic stopgap: **Ungoogled-Chromium** — near-zero version lag (152, tracks Chrome), **arm64 builds** (contributor AppImage, e.g. 148.0.7778.215), **AppImage no-install/no-root** (UOS has no root by default), **de-Googled** (fits data-residency compliance). **Caveats stated**: AppImage **cannot bundle glibc** (host-dependent), **UOS 20 is Debian-10-based with glibc 2.28** so newer builds may fail (`GLIBC_2.3x not found`) — must test per-machine (`ldd --version`); no ready 国密/UKey customization; not a certified catalogue product; self-managed updates. Recommendation: use it as a **complement** (web browsing / modern-web apps) alongside a certified vendor browser for business systems; and at ecosystem level, treat **kernel-version governance** (baselines, portable 国密/CA layer, security-debt accounting) as the real fix.
  - Key topics: Xinchuang, 信创, domestic OS, UOS, 统信, deepin, 360 信创版, 奇安信可信浏览器, Chromium, kernel version fragmentation, Chrome 2-week cadence, glibc 2.28, Debian 10, AppImage, arm64, Ungoogled-Chromium, 国密 SM2/SM3/SM4, UKey, CA trust chain, certification freeze

- [在 Linux 上原生跑安卓应用：Waydroid 实操与边界（不是模拟器，是容器化 LineageOS）](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-28_android-native-on-linux-waydroid/): Original deep-dive (not a translation) expanding the thesis "Android apps finally feel native on Linux, and I didn't need an emulator." **Waydroid** is the only realistic way to run Android apps on Linux and is **not an emulator** — it is a container/LXC-style scheme that boots an **Android 13 (LineageOS)** userspace **sharing the host Linux kernel** (so Android apps appear as native Wayland windows, not a nested VM). Hard prerequisites: **Wayland session** (Xorg unusable; can nest Weston or Cage for a Wayland session under Xorg) and a **kernel with binder support** (recommended: the community **Zen kernel**, which ships binder/Ashmem options on by default; otherwise self-compile with CONFIG_ANDROID_BINDER_IPC). Install path shown on **Arch via AUR** (init Waydroid, pull the LineageOS image, run the container under Wayland). GPU matrix is the biggest variable: **Intel** best / out-of-the-box, **AMD** mostly works but newer GPUs may require **self-building the Wayland image**, **Nvidia** historically problematic with an experimental dedicated Nvidia build still in development — otherwise slow software rendering. Best for users needing an Android-exclusive app or game on Intel/AMD + Wayland + binder kernel; not for Nvidia, hard Xorg-only, or conservative-kernel distros; default image lacks GMS (needs microG/signature handling). The "native feel" comes from the architecture (shared kernel, native windows), not a performance hack.
  - Key topics: Waydroid, Android on Linux, LineageOS Android 13, container not emulator, Wayland required, binder kernel, Zen kernel, Intel AMD Nvidia GPU matrix, Weston Cage nesting, microG, Linux desktop

On a **dual AMD EPYC 9575F** (64C/128T per socket, 5.0GHz boost / 4.5GHz all-core, 256MB L3 each) + **24×64GB DDR5-6400 = 1.5TB** + single **Samsung PM1743 Gen5 NVMe** (EXT4) on stock **Ubuntu 26.04 LTS** — no TMPFS/RAM-disk, no aggressive tuning — layering **Lorenzo Stoakes's Kbuild parallelization patch v4** (AI/LLM-assisted bottleneck hunting) dropped an x86_64 **defconfig** clean build from **~22s to 15–17s**, fastest **15s**; with **AMD power determinism** mode it hit 15s. **allmodconfig** shed **>30s**, nearing the **2-minute** mark on high-end servers. Phoronix's prior Kbuild work: Linux 7.4 builds ~36% faster clean / ~70% faster incremental. The "10 second" in the title is an expectation for the unreleased **EPYC 9686F (Venice)** (96C/192T, 5.0GHz, 384MB L3, MRDIMM-12800, PCIe Gen6) — **not yet achieved**. Key insight: with compilers still unable to parallelize a single .c file, the first lever for build time is Kbuild's parallelization quality, not core count — which is why the high-frequency 9575F beats higher-core parts. Takeaways: kernel is growing but builds are shrinking (software-side Kbuild parallelism + AI-assisted bottleneck finding, parallel to coding-assistants.rst / Sashiko); defconfig 15s / allmodconfig ~2min materially cuts bisect and full-module-verify iteration cost, and the gain is CPU-agnostic so it propagates downstream.

- [声卡整个消失了：一行 rm 删掉 .tplg，SOF 驱动找不到文件的全过程](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-23_sof-tplg-missing-no-soundcard/): Hands-on forensic write-up of a laptop that lost its entire sound card — speakers and microphones both gone, Bluetooth audio the only thing still working — on Debian 13 trixie with an XanMod 7.2.7 kernel and an Alder Lake-P HDA controller. Root cause: a single `sudo rm` had deleted `/usr/lib/firmware/intel/sof-tplg/sof-hda-generic-2ch.tplg`. The SOF driver's existence pre-check (`sof_test_topology_file()` calling `firmware_request_nowarn()`) failed, `sof_probe_work` returned `err: -2` (ENOENT), and no `snd_card` was ever registered — `/proc/asound/cards` empty, `aplay -l` reporting `no soundcards found`, PipeWire falling back to an `auto_null` sink, while `lspci -nnk` still showed `sof-audio-pci-intel-tgl` as `Kernel driver in use` (the distinction between "driver never loaded" and "driver probe failed late"). Bluetooth survived because it rides an independent USB / HCI / A2DP path that never touches either the Intel HDA controller or SOF — the failure domain simply did not reach it. The article then dissects the full mechanism of how the kernel locates and reads the file. (1) The filename is assembled in three parts: the base name `sof-hda-generic` comes from `snd_soc_acpi_intel_hda_machines[]`, the `-2ch` suffix is computed at runtime by `hda_machine_select()` in `sound/soc/sof/intel/hda.c` when `tplg_quirk_mask & SND_SOC_ACPI_TPLG_INTEL_DMIC_NUMBER` is set and the DMIC count is read from the BIOS-provided NHLT table (the `DMICs detected in NHLT tables: 2` line in dmesg), and the `intel/sof-tplg` prefix comes from `sof_dev_desc->default_tplg_path[ipc_type]` in `sof-pci-dev.c`. Practical consequence: the `-2ch` suffix is not your choice but the BIOS's — a firmware update changing the NHLT DMIC count to 4 would make the kernel look for `-4ch.tplg` and silently bypass any edits made to the `-2ch` file; `snd_sof_intel_hda_common dmic_num=N` can force an override. (2) SOF probes the file's existence before loading it: `sof_test_topology_file()` calls `firmware_request_nowarn()` and immediately `release_firmware()` if found. On failure it calls `sof_print_missing_firmware_info()`, which is the origin of the easily-misread message block `SOF firmware and/or topology file not found.` / `Supported default profiles` — that code lists every file expected for the IPC type (both `.ri` and `.tplg`), so seeing both listed does not mean both are missing; only the return values of `sof_test_firmware_file()` / `sof_test_topology_file()` decide, which is why the error text hedges with "and/or". (3) `fw_get_filesystem_firmware()` in `drivers/base/firmware_loader/main.c` tries a fixed `fw_path[]` array — the `firmware_class.path=` kernel parameter, `/lib/firmware/updates/$(uname -r)`, `/lib/firmware/updates`, `/lib/firmware/$(uname -r)`, `/lib/firmware` (note `/lib` is a symlink to `/usr/lib` on this system) — each retried with the empty, `.zst`, then `.xz` suffix, plus `firmware_fallback_platform()` for a UEFI-embedded copy: 15 candidates in strict order, `.zst` before `.xz`. Reads use `kernel_read_file_from_path_initns()`, i.e. with kernel credentials inside the init mount namespace, which is why granting a user read permission is useless and why no chroot or relogin is needed after fixing the file. (4) Measured `.tplg` structure: a 36-byte `struct snd_soc_tplg_hdr` (magic / abi / version / type / size / vendor_type / payload_size / index / count) followed by a variable-length payload, repeated. The verified file is 44247 bytes, 27 blocks, all with ABI 5, closing exactly at 43815 + 396 + 36 = 44247 — no residual bytes. Magic `0x41536F43` lands in the byte stream little-endian as ASCII `CoSA`, i.e. `ASoC` reversed. Block types present: 10 DAPM_GRAPH, 14 DAPM_WIDGET, 1 PCM (7 PCMs), 1 MANIFEST, 1 BACKEND_LINK (6 links). The kernel parser `snd_soc_tplg_component_load()` in `sound/soc/soc-topology.c` is not a single sequential pass but makes eight passes (MANIFEST, VENDOR, CONTROL, WIDGET, PCM_DAI, GRAPH, BE_DAI, LINK) because blocks are not guaranteed to be ordered. (5) ABI validation compares only the MAJOR number (`SOF_ABI_VERSION_INCOMPATIBLE` in `include/uapi/sound/sof/abi.h`), so `Topology: ABI 3:22:1 Kernel ABI 3:23:1` is normal backward compatibility (firmware package 2025.01 against a 2026 kernel); only a MAJOR mismatch is fatal, and fixing that requires a different `firmware-sof-signed` release. The package version determines file contents, never the filename — the name is computed by the kernel. (6) Load ordering explains the counter-intuitive symptom: `snd_sof_probe` → `sof_machine_check` → `sof_select_ipc_and_paths` (where the pre-check fails) → load `sof-adl.ri` → `snd_sof_run_firmware` boots the DSP → register the component → `snd_sof_machine_register` → only then `snd_soc_tplg_component_load()`. The topology is not part of the firmware, so a missing `.tplg` never stops the DSP from booting; it prevents the `snd_card` from being created, surfacing as `error: sof_probe_work failed err: -2`. Fix requires no reboot: restore the file and hot-reload via `echo 0000:00:1f.3 > /sys/bus/pci/drivers/sof-audio-pci-intel-tgl/unbind` then `.../bind`. The reason the reload is clean is that the failed probe leaves the device at `SOF_FW_BOOT_NOT_STARTED` (`sof_set_fw_state` at the end of the error path), so `snd_sof_device_remove()` takes the lightweight branch and never touches the DSP power domain or the i915 wakeref — a device that never succeeded is the safest to reload, whereas a device in `BOOT_COMPLETE` triggers the full teardown path that historically had a wakeref leak (fixed by the "Add remove_late() to sof_init_environment failure path" patch). Because `CONFIG_SND_SOC_SOF_PROBE_WORK_QUEUE=y`, probe runs in `sof_probe_work` asynchronously, so the `bind` write returning does not mean probe finished — the only valid verdict is `aplay -l` showing `card 0`. Two traps documented: (a) the `.bak` file sitting next to it was byte-identical to the `-pdm1` variant (`md5 91e6e760a72927deafe158efe29c9572`), because it snapshotted an already-overwritten file — rolling back to it would have traded "no sound card" for "one fewer microphone"; the authoritative test is `dpkg -V firmware-sof-signed` (`missing` means deleted, a `5` checksum mismatch means modified), and the pristine file (`md5 ef04df1833429c628a71a852bc83e4a4`) can be re-extracted with `apt-get download firmware-sof-signed` + `dpkg-deb -x`; (b) "file exists but content is wrong" and "file does not exist" are different failure modes — the former yields devices with wrong sound, the latter fails the pre-check and registers no card at all, which is why repeated topology-swapping attempts were the wrong direction. Also noted: `hda_dsp_hdmi_build_controls: no PCM in topology for HDMI converter 3` is benign noise (the `-2ch` topology has no PCM node for HDMI converter 3 while the ALC256 codec reports three HDMI converters) and must not be used as a reason to change topologies.
  - Key topics: SOF, Sound Open Firmware, ALSA, ASoC, `.tplg` topology, `sof-hda-generic-2ch.tplg`, firmware loader, `fw_path[]` search order, `.zst`/`.xz` decompression, `kernel_read_file_from_path_initns`, `snd_soc_tplg_hdr`, `SND_SOC_TPLG_MAGIC` (CoSA), `snd_soc_tplg_component_load` eight-pass parsing, `SOF_ABI_VERSION_INCOMPATIBLE` MAJOR-only check, NHLT table, `SND_SOC_ACPI_TPLG_INTEL_DMIC_NUMBER`, `hda_machine_select`, `sof_probe_work`, `CONFIG_SND_SOC_SOF_PROBE_WORK_QUEUE`, sysfs driver bind/unbind hot reload, `dpkg -V`, PipeWire `auto_null`, Debian 13 trixie, XanMod kernel
  - Diagnostic commands: `aplay -l`, `arecord -l`, `cat /proc/asound/cards`, `lspci -nnk -s 00:1f.3`, `journalctl -k -b | grep -E 'sof|snd_hda'`, `dpkg -V firmware-sof-signed`, `dpkg-deb -x firmware-sof-signed_*.deb /tmp/extract`, `md5sum /usr/lib/firmware/intel/sof-tplg/sof-hda-generic-2ch.tplg`, `ls /sys/module/snd_sof/parameters/`, `echo 0000:00:1f.3 > /sys/bus/pci/drivers/sof-audio-pci-intel-tgl/unbind`, `wpctl status`
- [DMS 换 Noctalia：niri 桌面壳迁移实录，以及两者的真实差别](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-22_dms-to-noctalia-niri-shell/): Hands-on migration record moving the desktop shell on Debian 13 + niri 26.04 from DankMaterialShell (DMS) 1.6 to Noctalia 5.1, plus an architecture comparison and pros/cons of each. Key facts (all verified on the machine): DMS 1.6.0db1 is driven by a statically-linked Go main binary (71 MB, `file` reports go1.26.5 statically linked) with Quickshell 0.3.0 (Qt6/QML, 12 libQt6 deps) as the UI layer; Noctalia 5.1.0 is pure C++ on Wayland + OpenGL ES with zero Qt/GTK dependencies (`ldd | grep -ciE 'qt|gtk'` = 0), a 7.7 MB deb extracting to 26 MB. Noctalia v4 was Quickshell-based but is deprecated (official docs: "v4 (Quickshell) is no longer maintained"); v5 is a full rewrite with separate config, coexisting with DMS. apt install simulation: only 3 new packages (noctalia, noctalia-data, fonts-noctalia-tabler), 0 upgrades, 0 removals, no Conflicts/Replaces/Breaks. Three counter-intuitive pitfalls hit during migration: (1) mako's notification daemon is D-Bus activated (cgroup `dbus-:1.1-org.freedesktop.Notifications@0.service`) via `/usr/share/dbus-1/services/fr.emersion.mako.service`, bypassing systemd, so masking `mako.service` is useless — the fix is a user-level override under `~/.local/share/dbus-1/services` pointing at `/bin/false`; (2) the real owner of `org.freedesktop.Notifications` turned out to be DMS itself (PID 71185), not mako, so query `GetNameOwner` before deciding what to stop; (3) `/usr/share/noctalia/assets/templates/niri/niri.kdl` contains `{{colors.*}}` mustache placeholders, and since niri's `include` fails hard, `niri validate` aborts with `invalid unknown format` — a static-color file must be generated first. Source-level finding: niri only runs `spawn-at-startup` once at launch (`src/main.rs`); `State::reload_config()` (`src/niri.rs:1546`) contains zero `spawn_at_startup` hits, so switching shells via hot reload requires manually launching the new shell. Noteworthy design difference: DMS auto-generates and overwrites ten `AUTO-GENERATED` files under `~/.config/niri/dms/` and injects an include into `config.kdl` (even overriding user layout values such as `gaps 6` → `gaps 4`), whereas Noctalia is explicitly non-invasive: "does not manage your compositor settings or take over your dotfiles." Post-switch verification: `listening on org.freedesktop.Notifications`, Intel Iris Xe OpenGL ES 3.2 / Mesa 25.0.7, bars generated on both DP-4 and eDP-1, i18n zh-Hans, `logind session lock monitor active` — with zero windows lost throughout (hot reload, no logout). Panel ids must be probed rather than guessed: `noctalia msg panel-open <bad-id>` reveals the available list (clipboard, control-center, launcher, polkit, session, setup-wizard, test, tray-drawer, wallpaper).
  - Key topics: niri, Wayland, Noctalia, DankMaterialShell, DMS, Quickshell, Qt6, C++, OpenGL ES, Debian 13 trixie, desktop shell, D-Bus activation, org.freedesktop.Notifications, mako, ext-session-lock, layer-shell, spawn-at-startup, KDL, mustache template, dotfiles
  - Diagnostic commands: `ldd /usr/bin/noctalia | grep -ciE 'qt|gtk'`, `file /usr/bin/dms`, `niri validate -c ~/.config/niri/config.kdl`, `niri msg action load-config-file`, `noctalia msg status`, `noctalia msg panel-open <id>`, `dbus-send --session --print-reply --dest=org.freedesktop.DBus /org/freedesktop/DBus org.freedesktop.DBus.GetNameOwner string:org.freedesktop.Notifications`

- [Gzip 1.15 发布：修了几个「自诞生起就存在」的 bug，其中一个是文件删除竞态](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-20_gzip-115-bugfixes/): Translation+analysis of Phoronix's report (Michael Larabel, 2026-09-20) on Gzip 1.15 succeeding 1.14 (April 2025). 100+ commits, mostly bug fixes collected over ~18 months, several bugs present since the project's inception. Fixes (quoting the GNU announcement): a TOCTOU where gzip could delete the wrong file if another process simultaneously renames an ancestor directory of the gzip destination; `gzip -d` no longer rejects PKZIP signatures/local headers/data descriptors found in well-formed streamed zip files; diagnostics now quote filenames with unusual characters; an uninitialized-memory use on some malformed inputs; a buffer overflow when decompressing an `.lzh` file after a `.Z` file; `.lzh` output corruption when an internal bit buffer was not cleared, and corruption from a previous file's decoding table on consecutive `.lzh` decompressions; `--synchronous` failing to sync unreadable parent directories on O_PATH (Linux) / O_SEARCH (FreeBSD) platforms (bug from 1.7); and a temp-file race in `gzexe`/`zdiff`/`znew` on platforms lacking `mktemp`. Also: gzip now follows the locale from the environment (no longer assumes C), and drops support for FreeBSD 4.11, HP-UX 11.00, Minix 3.1.8, and Windows 8.1 via non-UCRT MinGW. Takeaways: these aren't cosmetic — the `.lzh` buffer overflow and uninitialized-memory use are memory-safety issues exploitable via crafted untrusted input, and the TOCTOU matters for any script that uses gzip for cleanup/temp handling; the "since the beginning" bugs show cold legacy decompression paths (`.lzh`/`.Z`) get little audit despite billions of daily calls; as a pure-fix release with no breaking features and retired ancient platforms, 1.15 is a no-reason-to-delay upgrade, especially on multi-tenant / untrusted-input boundary nodes.
  - Key topics: gzip, GNU, compression, 1.15, bug fixes, buffer overflow, uninitialized memory, TOCTOU, data corruption, gzexe, locale, security operations

- [把 eBPF 安全代理的内核 CPU 开销砍掉 90%：靠的是记忆化，不是 AI](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-14_ebpf-memoization-90-percent/): Translation+analysis of nathan naveen's blog (2026-09-11). An eBPF file-open LSM security agent caches per-inode policy decisions in a `BPF_MAP_TYPE_LRU_HASH` (max_entries 10000); key = mntns_id + mount_id + inode (inode numbers only unique per mount tree, mntns prevents cross-namespace reuse), value = access_index (bitmask) + state. Benchmark: same file opened 200,000 times, kernel cycles dropped from 28B to 3.03B (~90%); `is_restricted_filepath`/`path_check_callback` fell to ~0.02% of stack (perf cycles:k). Edge case: hardlinks share an inode, so when `i_nlink != 1` the cache is skipped and it falls back to the slow path — correctness over hit rate. Repo: bomfather/agent.
  - Key topics: eBPF, LSM, memoization, BPF_MAP_TYPE_LRU_HASH, inode cache, hardlink, i_nlink, performance, dentry, mount namespace

- [rspamd 把 46% 的合法邮件丢进了垃圾箱：一次从配置文件体系开始的排查](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-23_rspamd-false-positive-tuning/): Hands-on false-positive audit of a self-hosted mail gateway (Debian 12 + postfix + dovecot + rspamd 4.2.0), with a systematic walkthrough of rspamd's five-layer configuration system (`rspamd.conf` top-level orchestration; `local.d/` per-key merge vs `override.d/` whole-section strict override; `scores.d/` + `groups.conf` symbol weights; `actions.conf` score thresholds; `modules.d/`, `settings.conf`, `rspamd.local.lua`, `maps.d/` as extension points). Measured outcome: legitimate mail misfiled to Junk dropped from 294/643 (46%) to 40/643 (6%), and per-message scan time from ~4136 ms to 611-1236 ms. Five stacked root causes: (1) `/etc/rspamd/options.inc` had been truncated to 25 lines from the packaged 93 (`options.inc.dpkg-dist`), dropping `filters = "chartable,dkim,regexp,fuzzy_check"`. rspamd's own docs state C modules are enabled only via the `filters` attribute and "if no filters attribute is defined, all C modules are disabled"; these are statically linked into `librspamd-server.so` (`nm -D | grep -ci dkim` = 31, `src/plugins/dkim_check.c` present) with no `.lua` file on disk, so nothing is visible in a file listing. Consequence: `R_DKIM_ALLOW`/`NA`/`REJECT` never registered, silently disabling `WHITELIST_DKIM`, `WHITELIST_SPF_DKIM`, `WHITELIST_DMARC`, `TRUSTED_NEWSLETTER_PASS`, `DMARC_CHECK` and `NO_AUTH_SPOOF` — while `configtest` still printed `syntax OK` with only `destination ... is missing` warnings. The same stub also dropped `dns{timeout=1s;sockets=16;retransmits=5}` and `local_addrs`; rspamd.log showed 1304 `query timed out` per day (concentrated on `asn6.rspamd.com` and DNSWL/URIBL zones), suppressing negative signals such as `DWL_DNSWL_HI` (-3.5). (2) `override.d/policies_group.conf` is priority=10 strict override, and its 28-line version omitted all six `R_DKIM_*` weights, yielding `R_DKIM_ALLOW has no score registered` — a case where `local.d/` (per-key merge) was the correct tool and `override.d/` was not. (3) `FORGED_SENDER` (+5.0) fires whenever envelope `MAIL FROM` and header `From` are not the same mailbox (`same_mailbox()` in `forged_recipients.lua`), which is exactly how every ESP works by design: `publishing@email.mckinsey.com` / `bounce@email.mckinsey.com`, `jobs-noreply@linkedin.com` / `m-1but2tww...@bounce.linkedin.com`, `notifications@github.com` / `bounces@sgmail.github.com`, and VERP mailing lists `author@debian.org` / `bounce-debian-list=user=freelamp.com@lists.debian.org`. In a 3687-message archive, 1785 messages had an envelope domain different-but-related to the header domain and every one was legitimate, zero spam; rspamd's built-in `ENVFROM_PRVS` only matches `prvs=`, `btv1==`, `msprvs1=` and had 0 hits in production. Fixed by a custom Lua symbol `RELAY_ENVELOPE` (score -5.0): envelope domain organisationally related to the header domain AND envelope shaped like a relay AND at least one of SPF/DKIM/DMARC passing; offline coverage of legitimate mail reached 98.5% (2426/2463). The authentication condition is load-bearing — without it a genuine unauthenticated spoof whose domains happen to be related would be waved through. (4) A `force_actions` rule named `BLOCK_SPOOFED_LOCAL_DOMAIN` used the expression `FORGED_SENDER & !DMARC_POLICY_ALLOW & !R_SPF_ALLOW` — which contains no local-domain test at all — so it hard-rejected any message whose envelope differed from its From and lacked SPF/DMARC; production showed 32 forced rejects, 22 of them legitimate `lists.debian.org` posts where `freelamp.com` was merely a VERP tag. Replaced by a Lua symbol `SPOOFED_LOCAL_DOMAIN` that genuinely checks the header From domain against `LOCAL_DOMAINS` and requires SPF, DKIM and DMARC all to have failed plus a non-authenticated, non-local origin. Note: `force_actions.lua` ignores an `enable` key (its rules loop reads only `sett.action` and `sett.expression`), verified by configtest, so the block must be commented out rather than disabled. (5) A global Dovecot Sieve script gated Junk filing on `X-Spam: Yes`, but that header is generated by `milter_headers.lua`'s `x-spam-status` routine under the condition `action ~= 'no action' and action ~= 'greylist'`, making its real threshold `add_header = 6` in `actions.conf`, not `reject = 15` — collapsing the entire 6-to-15 band into a binary verdict. Rewritten to test `X-Rspamd-Action` for `reject`/`rewrite subject` or `X-Spamd-Bar` with eight `+` (one per point). Regression methodology and three traps: `dovecot-keywords` is a per-mailbox index map (the same letter means `NonJunk` in INBOX but something else in another folder, so cross-applying one map inverts the labels and flips the conclusion); re-scanning Maildir breaks DKIM body hashes because stored messages use LF rather than the original CRLF, making `R_DKIM_REJECT` an artifact — judge real DKIM verdicts from `rspamd.log` instead; and rspamd re-reads the `X-Spam: Yes` header it wrote on the previous pass, triggering `SPAM_FLAG` for a spurious +5.0, so self-generated headers must be stripped before any rescan. Bottom line: a passing `configtest` does not mean the checks are running — verify with `rspamc counters` that the symbols actually exist.
  - Key topics: rspamd, postfix, dovecot, spam filtering, false positives, mail gateway, DKIM, SPF, DMARC, Sieve, FORGED_SENDER, ESP bounce address, VERP, local.d vs override.d, actions.conf thresholds, rspamd.local.lua, configtest, Debian 12
  - Diagnostic commands: `rspamadm configtest`, `rspamc counters | grep R_DKIM`, `rspamc stat`, `diff /etc/rspamd/options.inc /etc/rspamd/options.inc.dpkg-dist`, `nm -D /usr/lib/rspamd/librspamd-server.so | grep -ci dkim`, `wc -l /etc/rspamd/{scores.d,override.d}/policies_group.conf`, `journalctl -u opendkim -u rspamd`, `sieve-test <script> <message.eml`, `doveadm fetch`, `cat /path/dovecot-keywords`

- [Rembrandt：10 天做出一个 Lightroom 替代品，而它的 README 自己交代了原型来自 darktable](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-09_rembrandt-photo-editor-github/): Analysis of the Rembrandt photo editor (thesnarkitecht/rembrandt), a GPL-3.0 cross-platform Lightroom alternative with no account, no subscription, no tracking, on-device AI and optional self-hosting, presented through repository metrics measured via the GitHub API on 9 October 2026: created on 29 September 2026, 75 commits, a single contributor, 78 stars, and ten releases in ten days (v0.3.10 published 9 October) with 19 assets each. Covers the stack (JavaScript with WebGL2 and WebGPU shaders for the editing engine and on-device AI, a small Rust/Tauri desktop shell, and LibRaw compiled to WebAssembly for RAW decoding), the model support (Lensfun's 1,500 lens profiles, Real-ESRGAN for super resolution, KAIR/FFDNet for denoise via ONNX-style intermediates, and MediaPipe for subject, depth and object masks), and the notable engineering choices: the 'Ask in words' feature is explicitly 'a vocabulary, not a language model' running on device, originals are never moved or rewritten with edits saved as standard XMP sidecars readable by Lightroom and darktable, every release is built by GitHub Actions with SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance from 0.3.8, the updater verifies SHA-256 and never requests administrator rights, and the GPL includes an additional section 7 permission for app store distribution. Documents the key disclosure surfaced on Hacker News, where the author confirms in the README credits and in comments that the scene-referred design is modelled on darktable and that his first prototype ported some darktable algorithms before being replaced with an independent implementation prior to release, noting both projects are GPL-3.0 and crediting darktable directly. Reports the counterarguments from the discussion: a professional photographer counting at least ten similar AI-assisted photo editors in the past year that all remain rough around the edges compared with projects built over years, criticism that the author had to ask an LLM whether the workflow was darktable-inspired, concern about entrusting a photo library to a single-maintainer ten-day-old project, and the author's answer that originals are never modified and edits are open XMP so nothing is locked in if the project stops. Frames the wider issue of AI clean-room reverse engineering raised in the thread: implement cost has collapsed while legal standards are unchanged and auditability has fallen, so it is hard to assess a claim of independent implementation. Notes the licence details in NOTICE.md (LibRaw LGPL-2.1, MediaPipe Apache-2.0, Real-ESRGAN BSD-3, NSFWJS MIT, Lensfun database CC BY-SA 3.0, RAWmakase MIT) and the published methods the engine implements, observes that the installers are not yet code-signed, and closes with the recommendation to trial it read-only rather than entrusting a library initially.

- [LibreOffice 说「没有 AI」是个功能：但真正的价值是它给了六条验收标准](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-08_libreoffice-no-ai-feature/): Translation+analysis of The Document Foundation's 'no AI is now a feature' position, sourced from the original TDF community blog post rather than the media summaries. - [F-Droid 2.0 发布：十年最大改版，重写为 Kotlin Compose，安装体验终于追上系统商店](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-24_fdroid-2-0-release/): Translation+analysis of F-Droid's official blog (2026-09-24). F-Droid 2.0 is a complete redesign of the official Android app — the **largest update in 10 years**, after 14 test releases, rolling out over the coming weeks. Navigation is simplified into **Discover / Search / My Apps**; categories are greatly expanded and refined (VPNs, firewalls, password managers, launchers, navigation; the **Games** category reworked into **17 genres**) with higher-level "meta" categories; **search** now covers descriptions, categories and translated content (major improvements for **CJK/Chinese-Japanese-Korean** users, remembers recent queries); multi-criteria **filtering** (category, device compatibility, anti-features — e.g. device-compatible Action games excluding apps that depend on non-free network services) plus onboarding. **Install experience**: thanks largely to the EU's **Digital Markets Act (DMA)** and antitrust pressure, Android now offers all stores a smoother path; F-Droid 2.0 uses a **unified installer** and the new **pre-approval API** so users confirm right after deciding to install (not after download), bringing it close to the built-in store. Changes/removals: **updates fetch and install by default** (the **best refresh button is the one you never press**); pull-to-refresh is now scroll-only (manual trigger moved to the My Apps overflow menu); reworked data-usage settings; **Tor** simplified (auto-detection removed, "Use Tor" migrates to generic Proxy Settings, **Tor VPN** recommended); the **panic** feature stays; **app hiding simplified to only the icon and name** so users understand the disguise's limits (F-Droid still appears in Apps settings and is detectable in forensic inspection); the **app-wipe** feature (e.g. via the Ripple panic trigger) has **not returned** (specialized maintenance, small user base — users relying on it may postpone updating); **FPE is not supported by 2.0** which focuses on Android's **session installer** for background updates without it; OSes integrating F-Droid (CalyxOS, emteriaOS, iodéOS, Lineage-for-microG, ShiftOS) use additional repos. Under the hood: Kotlin + **Jetpack Compose**, closer to Material Design, **lowering the contributor barrier** and building a foundation for the next decade; support for **Android 6 was dropped** (a needed fix landed in Android 7) though old F-Droid releases still work on old Android. Funding: Torsten Grote's work via **NLnet/Mobifree**; **OTF UX & Discovery Lab** + **Ura Design** for user research/design; OTF FOSS Sustainability Fund, NGI, Mobifree, Calyx Institute; **OTF Security Lab + Convocation** independent security review. **Nearby** (serverless device-to-device app sharing) is being rebuilt on improved connection methods, not ready yet. Takeaways: (1) the install-experience gain comes from **antitrust/DMA pressure, not goodwill** — without regulation third-party stores stay second-class on Android; (2) Kotlin+Compose is a **strategic bet on lowering maintenance cost** for the next decade (cost: dropping Android 6, but old releases still work); (3) the privacy-feature trade-offs expose the **low-base/high-cost dilemma** of open-source projects, handled with honest boundary-setting and a downgrade path; (4) the backdrop is Google tightening sideloading vs the DMA forcing openness — F-Droid 2.0 lands in that window.
  - Key topics: F-Droid, Android, open-source app store, Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Material Design, DMA, Digital Markets Act, sideloading, privacy, app hiding, panic feature, Tor VPN, FPE, session installer, Nearby, CalyxOS, LineageOS, NLnet, Mobifree, Open Technology Fund
- [当软件订阅变成公共政策：一座城市的 70 万美元软件账单](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-24_software-subscriptions-public-policy/): Translation+analysis of O'Reilly Radar (Steve Hayes, 2026-09-24). A conversation with **Dan Gookin** — author of 1991's *DOS For Dummies* (the book that launched the *For Dummies* series; 180+ tech books, 12M+ copies) and now mayor of Coeur d'Alene, Idaho — becomes a bigger question: what happens when the software you *rent* becomes infrastructure you can't leave? Gookin: "Our software subscription just for our city, our size, is **$700,000 a year and growing**." His recurring example is the city's finance software — once *owned*, now leased and cloud-based — prompting: **"So we don't even own our own data?"** His worry isn't literal legal ownership but *practical control*: if the vendor is hacked or the city switches, can it get all its data back — "a binary dump" or the actual data? Gookin floats hiring a couple of contract programmers to rebuild in-house ("then we own it again"); Hayes is unconvinced: two programmers can't reproduce a mature municipal finance system, endpoint protection, records management and public-safety apps (let alone compliance and vendor support); AI-accelerated development adds liability/security risk a government likely won't accept in the name of ownership; in-house software creates its own long-term bills (maintenance, patching, staff/framework turnover); and an app you write can be **every bit as hard to escape as one you buy**. Conversely, replacing a "good enough" system with a packaged one that fits most-but-not-all of your needs can cost more than keeping the old one — build-versus-buy exists for good reasons. Still, the question stands: **at what point does the cost of renting capability justify rebuilding some of your own, and which capabilities should an organization insist on controlling even if renting is cheaper?** There's no universal answer, including "the vendor handles it." Hayes explicitly isn't arguing against the cloud — cloud/SaaS solve real problems (shifting maintenance to specialists; giving a 58,000-person city capabilities it could never economically build or maintain). The real question isn't cloud-vs-on-prem or proprietary-vs-open-source but whether you accept **dependency you've consciously chosen vs dependency you've acquired by default**; an org may rationally rent a critical service indefinitely — but it should know where the data lives, how it comes back, what switching would require, and which internal skills have atrophied. Takeaways: (1) at the individual level a subscription is a bill, but for governments/large orgs it's a **sovereignty / public-asset-control** question (public records' accessibility, portability and auditability bear on accountability); (2) the sharpest line is chosen-vs-default dependency, which escapes the cloud/local and open/proprietary binaries — the four questions are essentially an **exit plan** checklist; (3) it de-hypes "just build it yourself" and respects build-vs-buy — autonomy isn't free and isn't automatic, and owning your own code can be paid for in maintenance debt and harder-to-replace lock-in; (4) it rhymes with the broader rise of SaaS data-ownership/exit strategy, contractual data-portability clauses, "you own the code, you own the data" government advocacy, and AI-era context-data portability fights.
  - Key topics: software subscription, SaaS, public policy, vendor lock-in, data portability, exit plan, build vs buy, cloud, open source, government procurement, public records, dependency, O'Reilly Radar, Dan Gookin, Coeur d'Alene

- [Git 2.56 发布，3.0 要把 SHA-256 设为默认：reftable、强制 Rust 与大小写 ID 清除](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-18_git-256-and-30/): Translation+analysis of LWN's report (Jonathan Corbet, 2026-09-18) on Git 2.56 (RC, ~700 non-merge commits, ships late September: new `git history drop <commit>` that replays later commits but still refuses merge-containing histories, `git status` suggesting `git pull`, `git refs` create/delete/update/rename, `git branch --delete-merged`, `git add --resolved` that stages only conflict-resolved paths and aborts on leftover conflict markers, config-lock retry; routine fixes/refactors) and the likely Git 3.0 breaking changes. 3.0 candidates: SHA-256 becomes the default hash (replacing SHA-1; non-experimental since 2.42/2023; GitLab since 2024, Forgejo yes, GitHub the last forge gap but a SHA-256 repo was demoed at git-merge), reftable becomes the default ref storage (replacing `.git/refs` files, solves Android's 800k-ref inefficiency, libgit2 gained reftable support and defaulted SHA-256 in August), object IDs accept only lowercase (kills `f00f00` vs `F00F00` ambiguity bugs/vulns), and Rust becomes a hard build requirement from 3.0 (no-Rust-toolchain platforms can't upgrade; the Rust-free 2.99.x line gets long-term maintenance). Takeaways: the 3.0 breaking set is a single theme — paying down backward-compat debt (security, scale, maintainability, ambiguity removal); the SHA-256 default's real break point is forges not Git, eased by forward opt-in + full support for old SHA-1/reftable-less repos; forced Rust's blast radius is overstated and the 2.99.x line buys time; and the user-visible 2.56 wins are small commands (`history drop`, `add --resolved`, `branch --delete-merged`), with `history drop` still blocked by merges showing how many real histories carry merges.

- [CPO 的下一站，可能是一块玻璃：共封装光学走向「玻璃集成平台」](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-21_cpo-glass-integration-platform/): Translation+analysis of SemiWiki's piece (Moh Kolb, 2026-09-21) on co-packaged optics (CPO). CPO is framed as a proximity problem — move the optical engine next to the switch ASIC/XPU to shorten the electrical path, cut SerDes power, raise bandwidth density — but proximity doesn't eliminate the physical bottleneck, it just changes its coordinates in the system. Core thesis: packaging is no longer just supporting the system, it is defining what system can be built, and the substrate under CPO becomes strategic. Glass as an integration platform: good dimensional stability, low-loss high-frequency electrical routing, smooth surface for fine RDL, engineerable CTE, and much larger integration dimensions than wafer-constrained silicon interposers; because optics is geometrically sensitive, dimensional stability becomes an architectural capability. Further: future glass substrates could participate in both electrical and optical integration (TGV vertical vias + on-substrate optics) becoming an integration plane. The critical gate is TGV (through-glass via) manufacturing — via geometry, glass damage, metallization, copper fill, adhesion, residual stress, cracking, long-term reliability; glass is NOT a thermal material (thermal path must be deliberately engineered); and ecosystem (materials, equipment, TGV, fine RDL, KGD strategy, inspection, multi-source supply) matters more than the first demo. Pairs with the CXMT 3D NAND and Huawei 122TB SSD (board-level packaging) stories as the same "packaging breaks process limits / substrate inversion" narrative — advanced packaging is moving from sidekick to architecture definer.
  - Key topics: semiconductor, advanced packaging, CPO, co-packaged optics, glass substrate, TGV, heterogeneous integration, reftable-like ref storage, EIC/PIC, AI package, SemiWiki

- [Oracle 新一轮裁员：6 点清晨邮件、28 亿美元重组，以及 13% 的年度失血](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-09-14_oracle-layoffs-2-8b-restructuring/): Translation+analysis of TechTimes UK (2026-09-14). Oracle began a new layoff round sending termination emails at 6 a.m. Monday; FY2026 workforce fell ~21,000 (13%) to ~141,000 before this round. Restructuring plan cost raised by $700M to ~$2.8B (severance, contract termination, other costs). Reddit accounts describe a coordinated timeline: federated logins disabled 4 a.m. ET, Slack cut 5–5:30 a.m., emails at 6 a.m. sharp. Email text quoted ("today is your last working day"). Oracle has not said whether AI is absorbing eliminated roles and made no public comment on the round. Business Standard names Oracle/Amazon/Dell/Uber/PayPal as drivers of 2026 global layoffs.
  - Key topics: Oracle, layoffs, restructuring, $2.8B, workforce reduction, AI investment, TechTimes UK

## Quick Reference

### Linux TLS/PKI Commands
```bash
# Import private CA to system trust store (Debian/Ubuntu)
cp internal_ca.crt /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/
update-ca-certificates

# Verify certificate hash index
openssl x509 -in cert.pem -noout -hash

# Check Java trust store
keytool -list -keystore $JAVA_HOME/lib/security/cacerts

# Test TLS with custom CA bundle
curl --cacert /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt https://internal.service.local
```

### Network Diagnostics

- [TP-Link 首款 Wi-Fi 8 路由开启全球预售，美国被排除在名单外](https://freelamp.com/articles/2026-10-01_tplink-wifi-8-router-us-ban/): Translation+analysis of TP-Link opening global preorders for its first Wi-Fi 8 router, the Archer 8 Ultra, in the UK, Germany, Australia and others — with the United States left off the list. Without an FCC Conditional Approval, vendors are effectively barred from selling new wireless hardware in the US, so previously certified Wi-Fi 7 gear can still be sold while any new Wi-Fi 7 or Wi-Fi 8 product is locked out; TP-Link's move to incorporate TP-Link Systems in California is being challenged in legal filings. Specs: Broadcom Wi-Fi 8 chipset, up to 33 percent more real-world throughput than TP-Link's own Wi-Fi 7 hardware and 24 percent more consistent throughput under high interference, two auto-sensing 10 Gbps WAN/LAN ports, four 2.5 Gbps LAN ports, 3,600 sq ft coverage, 200 devices. Also covers the caveats that Wi-Fi 8 (802.11bn) is not yet ratified and this ships against a draft, so the upgrade only pays off once endpoints catch up.
  - Key topics: TP-Link, Archer 8 Ultra, Wi-Fi 8, 802.11bn, draft 2, FCC Conditional Approval, wireless hardware ban, TP-Link Systems, export controls, supply chain risk, Broadcom Wi-Fi 8 chipset, StabilityEngine, 10 Gbps WAN, mesh, Deco 8 Ultra, Roam 8, client-side device lag, 802.11n draft compatibility precedent
```bash
# Check DHCPv6 client status
systemctl status dhcp6c
journalctl -u odhcpd -n 50

# Verify IPv6 RA configuration
ip -6 route show default
rdisc6 -1 eth0
```
